exposure: delivery modes (vaginal delivery without episiotomy, vaginal delivery with episiotomy, cesarean section)
vertical distances between the location of bladder neck and the reference line of the inferior symphyseal margin at rest (BSDr)
cohort: The study included 738 primiparous women whose clinical and ultrasonographic data were collected.
finding: The independent relevant factors for postpartum urinary incontinence (PPUI) in primiparas varied with different delivery modes.
mod_finding: Independent factors associated with PPUI varied by delivery mode: BMI, BSDr, and RVAv were relevant for vaginal delivery without episiotomy, BND/BSDr for cesarean section, while no factors were independently associated with PPUI in the vaginal delivery with episiotomy group.
